title: Pacifico's racletteJS module is the right vehicle for a first co-built reference, not for volume
content:
The demo is a module inside racletteJS, Pacifico's own framework, dispatching typed operations from it. Building into a partner's own framework is the cheapest available seam: the maintainers control the extension point, and there is no third party to negotiate an upstream change with.

The research is careful about what that buys. Pacifico is described as small, fast and ideologically aligned — the three properties that make a first co-built reference feasible. It is explicitly not described as a route to volume, and the demo should not be read that way: its value is a working, jointly owned artefact and a public example, not a pipeline of deals.

Holding those two apart matters when the work is scheduled and reviewed. Judged as a channel play, the output will be measured in deals reached and will look like a failure; judged as a reference build, it succeeds by existing and by being something a later prospect can be pointed at.
